biggest_gaps: The new article is a how-to but never explains the 'why' behind steps (e.g. why cold wash, why pre-treat, why drum not drawer beyond 'too big') — the cup benchmark consistently explains the reasoning behind each instruction, which builds trust and usefulness.

Trade-offs section is thin and generic ('first few loads may feel odd'); the benchmarks name concrete scenarios (heavily soiled footy gear, oil stains, sensitive skin, hard water) so readers can self-qualify. Add specific load types where the ball underperforms.

No sourcing or caution framing. The cup benchmark cites a systematic review and TGA guidance and adds a 'general information only, not medical advice' line; the laundry benchmark at least quantifies the problem (10–13 bottles/year). The new article asserts 'natural minerals clean' with no supporting context or caveat about what 'natural minerals' means.
what_new_does_well: Excellent scannability: question-based H2s, a clean one-ball/two-ball table, and a FAQ block that directly mirrors likely search queries.
Honest, non-pushy framing — explicitly says the product may not suit people who want fragrance/softener and that this 'is fine', matching the benchmarks' no-pressure tone.
Accurate, disciplined use of supplied product facts (4 kg, 1,000 washes, sunlight recharge, recyclable outer ball) without inventing claims or dollar savings.
